market_summary: US equities are bifurcated: Nasdaq hit a fresh record (+0.5%) on AI-capex strength and cooling Fed-hike odds (18-20% after a soft 29k September jobs print), while the S&P (-0.3%) and Dow (-1.3%) lagged as 10-yr-equivalent yields spiked to a 2002-era high of 5.34% before retreating. That yield spike hit rate-sensitive assets hardest - Singapore's STI fell 1.3% on the week, with property/REITs and SGX itself getting hit. Mega-cap AI names (NVDA, TSLA, MSFT) continue to see strong price momentum and consensus-analyst upgrades, while SGX (the exchange operator) suffered an outsized single-day plunge on very heavy volume that stands out from the rest of the watchlist. Singapore's board-lot reduction (effective today) is a structural retail-access positive for local blue chips but is a slow-burn catalyst, not a near-term price driver.

picks.thesis: Nvidia just printed a fresh all-time high ($237.55 intraday, $5.7T market cap) on continued AI infrastructure capex from hyperscalers. Price is up 23% from July lows, trading 7% above its 50-day MA and only 0.8% off its 52-week high, with 58 of 61 analysts rating it Buy and a consensus target implying ~40% upside. Momentum plus an unusually one-sided analyst base supports continuation into year-end AI capex updates.
picks.news: Nvidia hit new intraday ATH ($237.55) and $5.7T market cap on Oct 2, 2026, extending a 23% rally from July lows amid continued hyperscaler AI capex.
picks.risks: Any sign of AI capex deceleration from major cloud customers, an export-control shock to China sales, or a broader de-rating of high-multiple tech (as the S&P/Dow divergence from Nasdaq already hints at some rotation away from megacaps) would hit NVDA hardest given its 1.59 beta and 37.6% annualized volatility.

picks.thesis: Tesla's Q3 deliveries of 486,532 beat consensus by ~5% and put the company on pace for its first annual delivery growth since 2023. The stock jumped 5.5-4.7% on the print and is now 6.6% above its 50-day MA with relative volume at 1.43x, suggesting fresh buying interest after a rough prior quarter (-11.7% 3m, -24.4% off 52w high), giving room for a relief/momentum continuation.
picks.news: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026 vs 461,974 consensus (beat by 5.3%), stock up ~5% on Oct 2, 2026; YTD deliveries up ~9% vs 2025.
picks.risks: TSLA remains the highest-beta (1.83) and highest-volatility (46.2% annualized) name on the list, with a mixed analyst split (19 buy/20 hold/4 sell) and still down 15% over the past year and 24% off its 52w high - a single soft margin print or price-cut headline could reverse the pop quickly.

picks.thesis: Microsoft is up 33.8% over 3 months and 6.1% above its 50-day MA, riding the same AI capex wave as Nvidia but with a far more one-sided analyst base (54 buy, 2 hold, 0 sell) and an 11.8% implied upside to consensus target. A recent Stifel upgrade (Hold→Buy, target raised to $575) on Sep 23 adds a fresh positive catalyst, and Microsoft's Azure/AI exposure benefits from the same capex tailwind pushing Nasdaq to records.
picks.news: Stifel upgraded MSFT from Hold to Buy with target raised from $530 to $575 on 2026-09-23 (stock +3.9% since); Nasdaq hit a record high on Oct 4, 2026 largely on AI-capex strength that benefits MSFT's cloud/AI business.
picks.risks: MSFT has the highest 1-year max drawdown on this list (34.9%) and flat 1-year return (+0.3%), showing it can reprice sharply; a slowdown in enterprise cloud spending or a hawkish Fed surprise (yields already spiked to 5.34% this week) would pressure the stock's rich multiple.

picks.thesis: Singapore Exchange plunged 7.2% in a single session on 4.35x normal volume, is now down 16% over the past month and 12.8% below its 50-day MA - a sharp technical breakdown distinct from the rest of the SGX watchlist (STI ETF only fell 1.3%). This kind of outsized, high-volume single-stock drop against a broadly calmer index often reflects a stock-specific negative catalyst (e.g., trading-volume/clearing-revenue concerns or index-related flows) that can continue to weigh on sentiment in the near term even though analysts still see ~15% upside to target.
picks.news: S68.SI fell 7.2% on Oct 4-5, 2026 with relative volume of 4.35x the 20-day average, amid a broader 1.3% STI decline driven by high US bond yields (growbeansprout.com weekly update, 2026-10-04).
picks.risks: If the drop was a one-off overreaction (e.g., to a single data point like softer securities turnover) rather than a structural issue, the stock could snap back quickly, especially given 6 of 16 analysts still rate it Buy with meaningful upside to the $24.12 consensus target.

picks.thesis: CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust is a rate-sensitive S-REIT that is already down 5.1% over the past year and sitting 5.5% below its 200-day MA. With US bond yields spiking to a 2002-high of 5.34% this week and Singapore property/finance names broadly underperforming (City Developments -14.8% on the week), REITs like CICT face continued valuation pressure from higher discount rates even though yields have since retreated somewhat.
picks.news: US bond yields spiked to 5.34% (highest since 2002) mid-week before retreating, pressuring Singapore property and rate-sensitive sectors; STI fell 1.3% with property names lagging (growbeansprout.com, 2026-10-04).
picks.risks: Conviction is low because yields already retreated from the week's peak, and 13 of 16 analysts still rate CICT a Buy with ~19% upside to target; a sustained decline in yields or a recession-driven Fed cut cycle would be bullish for REITs and invalidate this short.
